# Classes

One page per class, in order. Each class page has the slides, the video tutorials, the Blender example files, what to practice and what is due. Pages are posted as the semester reaches them. The midterm review is Week 10 — Oct 27.

## Graphic Standards Manual

Week 1. Establish the graphic system used to communicate all later work.

- [Class 01]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-01/) — Week 1 — Aug 25: Begin the Graphic Standards Manual, test a sample sheet and organize your files.

<a id="b02"></a>

## Constructive Solid Geometry

Weeks 2–3. Build editable solids with transformations and Boolean operations.

- [Class 02 · Transformations and Booleans]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-02/) — Week 2 — Sep 1: Move, rotate and scale procedurally. Compare solid Boolean operators and begin the massing study.
- [Class 03 · 3D printing]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-03/) — Week 3 — Sep 8: Refine the CSG process sheet and instructions. Introduce P2b: prepare the CSG object for 3D printing, including units, orientation and slicing.

<a id="b03"></a>

## Descriptive Geometry

Weeks 4–5. Describe geometry through points, lines, edges and faces, then build a parametric solid.

- [Class 04 · Point to solid]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-04/) — Week 4 — Sep 15: Point → Line → Edge → Face → Solid → Boolean. Build the parametric pyramid and reconnect to the CSG project.
- [Class 05 · Your module, material and lighting]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-05/) — Week 5 — Sep 22: Build your own module from points and faces, test its parameter ranges, then render it with one material and a deliberate lighting setup for the P3a sheet.

<a id="b04"></a>

## Arrays

Weeks 6–7. Two classes, two example files: 1D, 2D and 3D arrays in Week 6 (sheet 1); hexagonal, radial and curve arrays in Week 7 (sheet 2). A tutorial video is planned but not yet posted.

- [Class 06 · 1D, 2D and 3D arrays]({{ site.baseurl }}/modules/classes/class-06/) — Week 6 — Sep 29: 1D, 2D and 3D arrays: linear, nested grid and XYZ cube array, with index order and a conditional selection. Brief P3b; start sheet 1.
- Class 07 · Hexagonal, radial and curve arrays — *not yet released* — Week 7 — Oct 6: Hexagonal, radial and curve arrays, including a sine-driven curve. Start P3b sheet 2. No graded submissions during studio reviews.

<a id="b05"></a>

## Attractor

Weeks 8–9. Use distance fields from points and curves to control geometric variation.

- Class 08 · 2D field and plotter — *not yet released* — Week 8 — Oct 13: Attractors on a 2D field: measure distance, show the grayscale field, remap and clamp, then translate the field into lines, export an SVG and run a test plot. Brief P3c (plotter drawing) and P3d (site analysis).
- Class 09 · Site analysis with Mixtli — *not yet released* — Week 9 — Oct 20: Site analysis with the Mixtli add-on: pick a site, run an analysis, read it as a field and turn it into one design decision. Review P3c test plots. Midterm checklist.

<a id="b06"></a>

## Volumetric Data and Fields

Weeks 10–11. Read spatial samples, convert them into volumes and use fields to control form.

- Class 10 · Midterm review and SDF — *not yet released* — Week 10 — Oct 27: Present Projects 1-3: GSM, CSG diagram and print, module, arrays, plotter drawing and site analysis. Confirm the later schedule, then introduce volumetric data.
- Class 11 · SDF volume — *not yet released* — Week 11 — Nov 3: SDF volume: signed distance primitives, union/intersection/difference and smooth blends, noise and surface extraction. Brief P4a; select a volume for slicing.

<a id="b07"></a>

## Discretizing Geometry

Weeks 12–13. Use contours and sections to translate a volumetric design into parts for fabrication.

- Class 12 · Sections — *not yet released* — Week 12 — Nov 10: Slice the chosen volume into contours. Compare section directions, intervals and order.
- Class 13 · Parts for the laser cutter — *not yet released* — Week 13 — Nov 17: Develop section parts with thickness and registration. Test fit and kerf, then label and nest the parts.

<a id="b08"></a>

## Final

Weeks 14–15. Fabricate and assemble the work, document revisions and prepare the final booklet and review.

- Class 14 · Production — *not yet released* — Week 14 — Nov 24: Begin final production and assembly. Review fabrication tests, document revisions and develop the booklet.
- Class 15 · Documentation and booklet — *not yet released* — Week 15 — Dec 1: Fabricate and assemble sections within lab availability, then documentation, booklet and file checks. No graded submissions during the retained final studio-review window.

## Possible intermediate class

<a id="o01"></a>

**Tessellation, panelization, lattices and simulation.** Offered only if time allows after arrays or attractors; no separate submission. The file covers tessellation and lattices. Panelization and simulation are possible additions. [Optional example files]({{ site.baseurl }}/resources/example-files/)
